# Nibula

> Nibula is an open-source static site generator built on Eleventy, made for people moving from hand-written HTML to a real project setup.

Nibula is a command-line tool that generates ready-to-build Eleventy projects: it sets up folder structure, templates and configuration so you can start writing content immediately. Published on npm, Apache 2.0 licensed, maintained by Michele Garofalo.

## Documentation
- [Nibula · A gentler way into static site generators](https://rhaastrake.github.io/nibula/): Scaffold a complete Eleventy project — structure, SEO, server configs and an optional backend — while staying close to plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
- [Documentation · Nibula](https://rhaastrake.github.io/nibula/docs/v2/): Install Nibula, create your first project and learn the folder structure, components, styling, backend and deployment — with copy-paste examples throughout.
- [Documentation · Nibula](https://rhaastrake.github.io/nibula/docs/v3/): Install Nibula, create your first project and learn the folder structure, components, styling, backend and deployment — with copy-paste examples throughout.
- [FAQ · Nibula](https://rhaastrake.github.io/nibula/faq/): Answers to common questions about Nibula: supported Node versions, how it compares to other generators, backend options and troubleshooting.
- [About the project · Nibula](https://rhaastrake.github.io/nibula/team/): Who maintains Nibula, and how to contribute, report a bug or suggest a feature.
